svg.title: Privacy by Design (PbD) & Privacy-Enhancing Technologies Architecture
svg.desc: Three panels. All seven of Ann Cavoukian's Privacy by Design principles, grouped three to a line, as organizational design rules. Privacy-enhancing technologies — differential privacy, zero-knowledge proofs, homomorphic encryption, and secure multi-party computation — with the property each one bounds. A de-identification panel separating pseudonymization, which stays in GDPR scope, from anonymization, which is judged against a reasonable-means test rather than absolute impossibility.
svg.text: Ann Cavoukian's 7 Foundational Principles & Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs).
• 1–3. Proactive not reactive; privacy as the default setting; privacy embedded into design
• 4–5. Full functionality (positive-sum); end-to-end security across the full lifecycle
• 6–7. Visibility and transparency; respect for user privacy (keep it user-centric)
• Differential Privacy (ε, δ): Calibrated noise bounding what any single record contributes
• Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP): Prove statement truth without revealing underlying data
• FHE and SMPC: Compute over data no single party can read — at real performance cost
• Pseudonymization (GDPR Art. 4(5)): Replaces PII with tokens; reversible only with separate secret key
• Anonymization: Judged by whether re-identification is reasonably likely, not by absolute impossibility
• Data minimization: Collect strictly essential PII; enforce automatic retention expiry & secure deletion
PRIVACY LIFECYCLE: DEFAULT PRIVACY → DATA MINIMIZATION → PSEUDONYMIZATION → PET CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROTECTION
